{Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on surah 81, verses 1–14}

Upon his family and companions and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment. To proceed: we had reached, in our explanation of Juz' 'Amma, Surah al-Takwir, and here we begin it, God willing, in this session on Thursday, the first of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the year one thousand four hundred and thirteen (AH). We say:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾ ﴿When the sun is wound up (1), and when the stars fall (2), and when the mountains are set moving (3), and when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4), and when the wild beasts are gathered together (5).﴾ [al-Takwir 1–5].

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾. This will happen on the Day of Resurrection. Al-takwir (winding up): gathering a thing together and wrapping it, as a turban is wound around the head. The sun is a huge, great, vast mass; on the Day of Resurrection Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will wind it up, wrapping it entirely and folding one part over another, so its light departs, and He will cast it into the Fire, out of anger toward those who worshipped it besides Allah.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], meaning: you will be hurled into Hell. ﴿You are its certain entrants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Excepted from this are those who were worshipped besides Allah among the friends of Allah, for they will not be cast into the Fire, as Allah said after this verse: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it (101). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in what their souls desire (102).﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101–102].

﴿When the stars fall﴾: ﴿infatara﴾ (fall) means: they will drop, as the second verse explains: ﴿And when the planets are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar 2]. So on the Day of Resurrection the stars will be scattered and will leave their places.

﴿And when the mountains are set moving﴾: these great, hard, high and lofty mountains will become scattered dust on the Day of Resurrection and will be set moving, as Allah said: ﴿And the mountains will be set moving, becoming a mirage﴾ [al-Naba' 20].

﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: ﴿al-'ishar﴾ is the plural of 'ushara', the pregnant she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. She was among the most precious possessions for the Arabs; you find her owner watching over her, attending to her, caring for her, sheltering her, and tending to her in this world. But in the Hereafter she is abandoned and no one turns to her, because a person will be in a great, distressing matter that makes him forget everything, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother (34), his mother and his father (35), his wife and his children (36). For every one of them, on that Day, will be a matter that preoccupies him.﴾ [Abasa 34–37].

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾: ﴿al-wuhush﴾ is the plural of wahsh, and what is meant is all animals, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book; then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-An'am 38]. Animals will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, people will see them, and retribution will be exacted for some of them against others, to the point that retribution is exacted for the hornless animal against the horned one. When retribution has been exacted among these beasts, Allah, Exalted is He, will command them and they will become dust. He, glory be to Him, does this only to manifest His justice among His creatures.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir 6]: ﴿al-bihar﴾ is the plural of bahr (sea), and it is used in the plural because of its greatness and abundance, for they represent roughly three quarters of the earth or more. When the Day of Resurrection comes, these great seas will be set ablaze, meaning kindled with fire; they will burn with a great fire, and then the earth will dry up and no water will remain in it, since its seas, those great waters, will be set ablaze until they become fire.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir 7]: ﴿al-nufus﴾ is the plural of nafs (soul), and what is meant is the whole human being. The souls will be paired, meaning each category will be joined to its like, because zawj (pair) is used to mean a category, as Allah said: ﴿And you were three categories﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 7], that is, three kinds. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And others of similar kind [azwaj]﴾ [Sad 58], meaning kinds. And He said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions [azwajahum]﴾ [al-Saffat 22], meaning their kinds and their likenesses.

So on the Day of Resurrection each likeness will be joined to its like: the people of goodness to the people of goodness, and the people of evil to the people of evil. This Ummah will be joined together, and ﴿you will see every nation kneeling﴾ [al-Jathiyah 28], each by itself: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record: Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Jathiyah 28].

Therefore ﴿and when the souls are paired﴾ means they will be arranged and joined together, each category to its category, each nation to its nation.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked (8), for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir 8–9]. ﴿Al-mawudah﴾ is the female who is buried alive. This was in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah), because of their ignorance and bad opinion of Allah, and their unwillingness to bear the shame, when one of them was given a female child. When ﴿one of them is given the good news of a female, his face remains darkened and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ [al-Nahl 58]: full of worry and sorrow. ﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ [al-Nahl 59], meaning he hides from them, ﴿because of the evil of what he has been given good news of. Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?﴾ [al-Nahl 59].

That is: if one of them was told, "We give you good news that Allah has given you a female, a daughter," he would be distressed and anxious, filled with grief and worry, and begin to think whether he should keep this girl in humiliation and disgrace or bury her in the dust and be rid of her.

Some of them did this and some did that. Among them, may Allah protect us, were those who buried the girl alive, either before she could discern or after she could discern. Some would dig the pit for his daughter, and if some dust fell on his beard as he dug for her burial, he would shake it off his beard while doing so, and there was no mercy in his heart for her. This shows you that the state of the jahiliyyah was depraved, for wild beasts are tender toward their young, yet these people were not tender toward their children.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾: she will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿For what sin she was killed﴾: why was she killed? Had she committed a sin? If a person says: how can she be asked when she was the wronged one, the one buried, and she may have been buried before she could discern, and the pen of obligation had not been applied to her, so how can she be questioned? It is said: she is questioned as a rebuke to the one who buried her, because she is questioned in his presence, and it is said to her: "For what sin were you killed?"

A parallel to this: if one person transgressed against another in this world and they brought them to the ruler, the prince, and he said to the wronged one: "With what did this man strike you? For what sin did this man beat you?" while he knows that he was the one transgressed against and had no sin, but this is for the rebuke of the oppressor. So the buried girl is asked "for what sin were you killed" as a rebuke to her oppressor, her killer and her burier. We ask Allah for well-being.

﴿And when the scrolls are spread open﴾ [al-Takwir 10]. ﴿Al-suhuf﴾ is the plural of sahifah, which is that in which deeds are written.

Know, O human, that every deed you do, whether word or action, is written down. It is recorded in scrolls by the hands of noble, trustworthy scribes who know what you do. Everything you do is recorded. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Exalted is He, says in His Book: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾ [al-Isra' 13], meaning his deed is around his neck. ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra' 13]: open. ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra' 14].

Our speech now, as we speak, is being written; the words some of you say to others are written; every word is written: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer ready﴾ [Qaf 18]. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Part of the goodness of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him" [al-Tirmidhi (2318) from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both]. And he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6475), Muslim (47/74), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him], because everything will be written against him, and whoever talks much will have many slips; that is, one who talks a great deal will have much error and many stumbles. So guard your tongue, for the scrolls will record everything you say, and it will be spread open for you on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And when the scrolls are spread open (10), and when the sky is stripped away﴾ [al-Takwir 10–11]. The sky above us now is a firm, strong, well-protected ceiling. Allah said: ﴿And the sky We built with strength﴾ [al-Dhariyat 47], meaning with power, and He said: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾ [al-Naba' 12], meaning strong. On the Day of Resurrection it will be stripped away, that is, removed from its place, as the skin is stripped from a camel when it is flayed from the meat. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will strip it away, then fold it up with His right hand, Exalted is He, as Allah said: ﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 67], ﴿like the folding of the scroll for the writings﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104], meaning as the scroll folds the writings; that is, when the scribe finishes writing he folds the page to preserve it from tearing and from erasure.

So the sky will be stripped away on the Day of Resurrection and the matter will be an open expanse, except that Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will carry the throne of your Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah 17]. Instead of the sky above us now, what will be above us is the Throne, because the heavens will be folded by the right hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He will fold them with His right hand and shake them, and likewise the earth with the other hand, and He will say: "I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4812), Muslim (2787), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, whose wording is: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heavens with His right hand, then say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"].

﴿And when the Blazing Fire is set alight﴾ [al-Takwir 12]. ﴿Al-Jahim﴾ is the Fire, and it was named so for the depth of its bottom and the darkness of its sight, may Allah grant that He saves us and you from it. It is set alight, meaning kindled. What is its fuel with which it is kindled? Its fuel, about which Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Tahrim 6]. Instead of wood and paper being brought, the fuel will be people, meaning the disbelievers, and stones of a great fire, intensely flammable and intensely hot. This is the kindling of Hell.

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾ [al-Takwir 13]. Paradise is the abode of the righteous, containing what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿Brought near﴾ means brought close and adorned for the believers.

Consider the difference between this and that: the abode of the disbelievers, what is done to it? Answer: it is set alight and kindled. The abode of the believers is adorned and brought near. ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: all of this will happen on the Day of Resurrection.

When we recite these verses: ﴿When the sun is wound up (1), and when the stars fall (2), and when the mountains are set moving (3), and when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4), and when the wild beasts are gathered together (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8), for what sin she was killed (9), and when the scrolls are spread open (10), and when the sky is stripped away (11), and when the Blazing Fire is set alight (12), and when Paradise is brought near﴾: these are twelve clauses, and so far the answer has not come, because all of them are within the condition, ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾, so the answer has not yet come. What will happen when these things occur?

Allah said: ﴿A soul will know what it has presented﴾ [al-Takwir 14], meaning what it has sent ahead of good and evil. ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil﴾ [Al 'Imran 30], meaning it will also be presented. ﴿It wishes there were between it and that a great distance; and Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran 30]. So on that Day every soul will know what it has presented of good or evil.

In this world we know what we do of good and evil, but we quickly forget. Who now remembers what he did in the past since the pen of obligation was applied to him? We have forgotten much, of obedience and of sins alike. But do you think this has gone to waste just because we forgot it? No, by Allah, it remains, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, you will bring it forth by your own acknowledgment against yourself that you did it.

For this reason He said: ﴿A soul will know what it has presented﴾ [al-Takwir 14]. It is necessary, indeed obligatory, for a person to reflect on these great verses, to take admonition from what they contain, and to believe in them as if he sees them with his own eyes, because what Allah has informed us of and whose meaning we know is more certain to us than what we have witnessed with our eyes or heard with our ears, since the report of Allah does not deceive. True.

But what we see or hear is often subject to illusion: you may see a distant thing as a shape and identify it by your imagination while it is contrary to reality, and you may hear a sound and think it is some specific thing in your mind while it is contrary to reality. Illusion affects the senses, but the report of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, once its meaning is known, can never be subject to any illusion, because it is a true report.

These matters which Allah mentioned in these verses are real matters; you must believe in them as if you see them with your own eyes. Then, after believing in them, you must act according to what they indicate of admonition and restraint, performing what is obligatory and abandoning what is forbidden, so that you may be among the people of the Qur'an who recite it as it should be recited. May Allah make me and you among them by His bounty and generosity; indeed He is over all things competent.

The sun is a huge, great, vast mass; on the Day of Resurrection Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will wind it up, wrapping it entirely and folding one part over another, so its light departs, and He will cast it into the Fire, out of anger toward those who worshipped it besides Allah.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], meaning: you will be hurled into Hell. ﴿You are its certain entrants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Excepted from this are those who were worshipped besides Allah among the friends of Allah, for they will not be cast into the Fire, as Allah said after this verse: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it (101). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in what their souls desire (102).﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101–102].

﴿When the stars fall﴾: ﴿infatara﴾ (fall) means: they will drop, as the second verse explains: ﴿And when the planets are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar 2]. So on the Day of Resurrection the stars will be scattered and will leave their places.

﴿And when the mountains are set moving﴾: these great, hard, high and lofty mountains will become scattered dust on the Day of Resurrection and will be set moving, as Allah said: ﴿And the mountains will be set moving, becoming a mirage﴾ [al-Naba' 20].

﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: ﴿al-'ishar﴾ is the plural of 'ushara', the pregnant she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. She was among the most precious possessions for the Arabs; you find her owner watching over her, attending to her, caring for her, sheltering her, and tending to her in this world. But in the Hereafter she is abandoned and no one turns to her, because a person will be in a great, distressing matter that makes him forget everything, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother (34), his mother and his father (35), his wife and his children (36). For every one of them, on that Day, will be a matter that preoccupies him.﴾ [Abasa 34–37].

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered together﴾: ﴿al-wuhush﴾ is the plural of wahsh, and what is meant is all animals, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book; then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-An'am 38]. Animals will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, people will see them, and retribution will be exacted for some of them against others, to the point that retribution is exacted for the hornless animal against the horned one. When retribution has been exacted among these beasts, Allah, Exalted is He, will command them and they will become dust. He, glory be to Him, does this only to manifest His justice among His creatures.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir 6]: ﴿al-bihar﴾ is the plural of bahr (sea), and it is used in the plural because of its greatness and abundance, for they represent roughly three quarters of the earth or more. When the Day of Resurrection comes, these great seas will be set ablaze, meaning kindled with fire; they will burn with a great fire, and then the earth will dry up and no water will remain in it, since its seas, those great waters, will be set ablaze until they become fire.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir 7]: ﴿al-nufus﴾ is the plural of nafs (soul), and what is meant is the whole human being. The souls will be paired, meaning each category will be joined to its like, because zawj (pair) is used to mean a category, as Allah said: ﴿And you were three categories﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 7], that is, three kinds. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And others of similar kind [azwaj]﴾ [Sad 58], meaning kinds. And He said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions [azwajahum]﴾ [al-Saffat 22], meaning their kinds and their likenesses.

So on the Day of Resurrection each likeness will be joined to its like: the people of goodness to the people of goodness, and the people of evil to the people of evil. This Ummah will be joined together, and ﴿you will see every nation kneeling﴾ [al-Jathiyah 28], each by itself: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record: Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Jathiyah 28].

Therefore ﴿and when the souls are paired﴾ means they will be arranged and joined together, each category to its category, each nation to its nation.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked (8), for what sin she was killed﴾ [al-Takwir 8–9]. ﴿Al-mawudah﴾ is the female who is buried alive. This was in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah), because of their ignorance and bad opinion of Allah, and their unwillingness to bear the shame, when one of them was given a female child. When ﴿one of them is given the good news of a female, his face remains darkened and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ [al-Nahl 58]: full of worry and sorrow. ﴿He hides himself from the people﴾ [al-Nahl 59], meaning he hides from them, ﴿because of the evil of what he has been given good news of. Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?﴾ [al-Nahl 59].

That is: if one of them was told, "We give you good news that Allah has given you a female, a daughter," he would be distressed and anxious, filled with grief and worry, and begin to think whether he should keep this girl in humiliation and disgrace or bury her in the dust and be rid of her.

Some of them did this and some did that. Among them, may Allah protect us, were those who buried the girl alive, either before she could discern or after she could discern. Some would dig the pit for his daughter, and if some dust fell on his beard as he dug for her burial, he would shake it off his beard while doing so, and there was no mercy in his heart for her. This shows you that the state of the jahiliyyah was depraved, for wild beasts are tender toward their young, yet these people were not tender toward their children.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾: she will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿For what sin she was killed﴾: why was she killed? Had she committed a sin? If a person says: how can she be asked when she was the wronged one, the one buried, and she may have been buried before she could discern, and the pen of obligation had not been applied to her, so how can she be questioned? It is said: she is questioned as a rebuke to the one who buried her, because she is questioned in his presence, and it is said to her: "For what sin were you killed?"

A parallel to this: if one person transgressed against another in this world and they brought them to the ruler, the prince, and he said to the wronged one: "With what did this man strike you? For what sin did this man beat you?" while he knows that he was the one transgressed against and had no sin, but this is for the rebuke of the oppressor. So the buried girl is asked "for what sin were you killed" as a rebuke to her oppressor, her killer and her burier. We ask Allah for well-being.

﴿And when the scrolls are spread open﴾ [al-Takwir 10]. ﴿Al-suhuf﴾ is the plural of sahifah, which is that in which deeds are written.

Know, O human, that every deed you do, whether word or action, is written down. It is recorded in scrolls by the hands of noble, trustworthy scribes who know what you do. Everything you do is recorded. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Exalted is He, says in His Book: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck﴾ [al-Isra' 13], meaning his deed is around his neck. ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra' 13]: open. ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra' 14].

Our speech now, as we speak, is being written; the words some of you say to others are written; every word is written: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer ready﴾ [Qaf 18]. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Part of the goodness of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him" [al-Tirmidhi (2318) from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both]. And he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6475), Muslim (47/74), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him], because everything will be written against him, and whoever talks much will have many slips; that is, one who talks a great deal will have much error and many stumbles. So guard your tongue, for the scrolls will record everything you say, and it will be spread open for you on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And when the scrolls are spread open (10), and when the sky is stripped away﴾ [al-Takwir 10–11]. The sky above us now is a firm, strong, well-protected ceiling. Allah said: ﴿And the sky We built with strength﴾ [al-Dhariyat 47], meaning with power, and He said: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾ [al-Naba' 12], meaning strong. On the Day of Resurrection it will be stripped away, that is, removed from its place, as the skin is stripped from a camel when it is flayed from the meat. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will strip it away, then fold it up with His right hand, Exalted is He, as Allah said: ﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 67], ﴿like the folding of the scroll for the writings﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104], meaning as the scroll folds the writings; that is, when the scribe finishes writing he folds the page to preserve it from tearing and from erasure.

So the sky will be stripped away on the Day of Resurrection and the matter will be an open expanse, except that Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will carry the throne of your Lord﴾ [al-Haqqah 17]. Instead of the sky above us now, what will be above us is the Throne, because the heavens will be folded by the right hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He will fold them with His right hand and shake them, and likewise the earth with the other hand, and He will say: "I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4812), Muslim (2787), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, whose wording is: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heavens with His right hand, then say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"].

﴿And when the Blazing Fire is set alight﴾ [al-Takwir 12]. ﴿Al-Jahim﴾ is the Fire, and it was named so for the depth of its bottom and the darkness of its sight, may Allah grant that He saves us and you from it. It is set alight, meaning kindled. What is its fuel with which it is kindled? Its fuel, about which Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Tahrim 6]. Instead of wood and paper being brought, the fuel will be people, meaning the disbelievers, and stones of a great fire, intensely flammable and intensely hot. This is the kindling of Hell.

﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾ [al-Takwir 13]. Paradise is the abode of the righteous, containing what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿Brought near﴾ means brought close and adorned for the believers.

Consider the difference between this and that: the abode of the disbelievers, what is done to it? Answer: it is set alight and kindled. The abode of the believers is adorned and brought near. ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾: all of this will happen on the Day of Resurrection.

When we recite these verses: ﴿When the sun is wound up (1), and when the stars fall (2), and when the mountains are set moving (3), and when the pregnant camels are abandoned (4), and when the wild beasts are gathered together (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8), for what sin she was killed (9), and when the scrolls are spread open (10), and when the sky is stripped away (11), and when the Blazing Fire is set alight (12), and when Paradise is brought near﴾: these are twelve clauses, and so far the answer has not come, because all of them are within the condition, ﴿When the sun is wound up﴾, so the answer has not yet come. What will happen when these things occur?

Allah said: ﴿A soul will know what it has presented﴾ [al-Takwir 14], meaning what it has sent ahead of good and evil. ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil﴾ [Al 'Imran 30], meaning it will also be presented. ﴿It wishes there were between it and that a great distance; and Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran 30]. So on that Day every soul will know what it has presented of good or evil.

In this world we know what we do of good and evil, but we quickly forget. Who now remembers what he did in the past since the pen of obligation was applied to him? We have forgotten much, of obedience and of sins alike. But do you think this has gone to waste just because we forgot it? No, by Allah, it remains, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, you will bring it forth by your own acknowledgment against yourself that you did it.

For this reason He said: ﴿A soul will know what it has presented﴾ [al-Takwir 14]. It is necessary, indeed obligatory, for a person to reflect on these great verses, to take admonition from what they contain, and to believe in them as if he sees them with his own eyes, because what Allah has informed us of and whose meaning we know is more certain to us than what we have witnessed with our eyes or heard with our ears, since the report of Allah does not deceive. True.

But what we see or hear is often subject to illusion: you may see a distant thing as a shape and identify it by your imagination while it is contrary to reality, and you may hear a sound and think it is some specific thing in your mind while it is contrary to reality. Illusion affects the senses, but the report of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, once its meaning is known, can never be subject to any illusion, because it is a true report.

These matters which Allah mentioned in these verses are real matters; you must believe in them as if you see them with your own eyes. Then, after believing in them, you must act according to what they indicate of admonition and restraint, performing what is obligatory and abandoning what is forbidden, so that you may be among the people of the Qur'an who recite it as it should be recited. May Allah make me and you among them by His bounty and generosity; indeed He is over all things competent.

(...) We continue here what we discussed earlier from Surah at-Takwir, where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede, (15) that run and hide,﴾ [at-Takwir 15–16]. Allah's words ﴿So I swear﴾ may lead some people to think that "la" is a negation, but it is not. Rather, it is an affirmation of the oath, and it is used in this structure for emphasis.

So the meaning is: ﴿I swear by the stars that recede﴾. Al-Khunnas (the stars that recede) is the plural of khanisah, which refers to stars that recede, meaning they return. You see them high on the horizon, and then they are suddenly moving back toward the other horizon. This is, and Allah knows best, because of their height and distance, so the stars beneath them appear, to the eye, to move faster than them.

As for His words ﴿al-jawari﴾, the original form is (al-jawari) with a yā', but the yā' was dropped for lightness. Al-Kunnas are those that hide (yakunisu), that is, they enter into their setting. Allah swore by these stars, then He swore by the night and the day, saying: ﴿And by the night when it turns away, (17) and by the morning when it breathes,﴾ [at-Takwir 17–18].

As for the meaning of ﴿'as'asa﴾: it means it approached (aqbala). It was also said that it means it withdrew (adbara). The word ʿasʿasa in the Arabic language is suitable for both, but what appears to be its meaning is "it approached," to match and agree with what follows it of the oath, which is His words ﴿and by the morning when it breathes﴾.

So Allah swore by the night as it approaches, and by the day as it approaches. Allah the Exalted swore by these creations because of their greatness and because they are among His great signs. Who can bring the day when it is night, and who can bring the night when it is day?

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If Allah were to make the night continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen? (71) Say: Have you considered? If Allah were to make the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see? (72) And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas 71–73].

These great creations are the things Allah swears by, because of the greatness of what is sworn to, which is His words: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [at-Takwir 19]. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿The word of a noble messenger﴾ is Jibril (peace be upon him), for he is the messenger of Allah to the messengers, with the revelation that he sends down to them. Allah described him as noble because of his good appearance, as He said in another verse: ﴿Possessor of strength; so he stood firm﴾ [an-Najm 6]. ﴿Possessor of strength (dhu mirrah)﴾: the scholars said that mirrah means good character and beautiful form. So Jibril (peace be upon him) was described with this description, ﴿noble﴾.

﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne﴾ [at-Takwir 20]. ﴿Possessing power﴾: Allah described him with great strength. The Messenger ﷺ saw him in his true form, in which Allah created him, having six hundred wings, which filled the whole horizon because of his greatness (peace be upon him).

His words ﴿near the Lord of the Throne﴾ mean near the Owner of the Throne, who is Allah, glorified and exalted. The Throne is above everything, and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Raised in degrees, Owner of the Throne; He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 15]. So the Owner of the Throne is Allah.

His words ﴿makin﴾ mean possessing standing, meaning that Jibril is, with Allah, of standing and honor. For this reason Allah singled him out with the greatest of the blessings that Allah sent down to His servants, which is revelation. My brothers, if we look at blessings, we will find that they are of two kinds: blessings in which animals and humans are equal, which are the enjoyment of the body: eating, drinking, marriage, and shelter. Humans are equal to animals in these blessings. Is that not so? Humans enjoy what they eat, what they drink, what they marry, and where they live, and animals are likewise.

The other blessings, which are specific to humans, are the laws (sharai'), the laws that Allah sent down through the messengers so that the lives of creation may be upright, because the lives of creation cannot be upright or good except through the laws: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97].

The believer who does righteous deeds is the one who has a good life in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter. By Allah, if you searched through kings and the sons of kings, ministers and the sons of ministers, rulers and the sons of rulers, the wealthy and the sons of the wealthy, and if you searched them and searched those who believed and did righteous deeds, you would find the second to have the better life, the more content heart, and the more open chest. This is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, has guaranteed it. He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

You find the believer who does righteous deeds joyful of heart, open of chest, content with Allah's decree and destiny. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke the truth.

So the greatest blessing Allah sent down to creation is the blessing of the religion, by which the life of a person is sustained in this world and the Hereafter. Now I ask you: What is life? Is it the life of this world or the life of the Hereafter? It is the life of the Hereafter. The evidence is His words in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life"﴾... Complete the verse: ﴿[Fajr 24]﴾, ["I wish I had sent forth (good) for my life"] [al-Fajr 24].

So this world is nothing; true life is the life of the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter will live a good life in this world, as I recited the verse to you. Thus the believer who does righteous deeds is the one who gains both lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is the one who loses both this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne. (20) Obeyed there and trustworthy﴾ [at-Takwir 20–21]. ﴿Obeyed there﴾ means there (in the heavens), ﴿trustworthy﴾ in what he was entrusted with. Who obeys him? Jibril is the one who is obeyed, so who obeys him?

The scholars said: The angels obey him, because he descends with the command from Allah and then commands the angels, and they obey. So he has authority and obedience over the angels. Then the messengers (peace be upon them), to whom Jibril descends with revelation, have authority and obedience over the mukallafun (those obligated by the law). ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾ [al-Ma'idah 92].

﴿Obeyed there and trustworthy﴾. When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, swore that this Qur'an is the word of this noble messenger, the angelic one, in another verse Allah clarified and swore that this Qur'an is the word of a noble messenger, in His words: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (40) and it is not the word of a poet﴾ [al-Haqqah 38–41]. Is the messenger there the same as the messenger here?

The answer: No. The messenger here, in Surah at-Takwir, is an angelic messenger, meaning one of the angels, and he is Jibril. The messenger there is a human messenger, and he is Muhammad (peace be upon him).

The evidence for this is clear. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (19), possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne﴾. To whom does this description refer? To Jibril, the one who is with Allah. As for Muhammad (peace be upon him), he is on earth. There He said: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (40) and it is not the word of a poet﴾, in response to the saying of the disbelievers who said that Muhammad is a poet, ﴿nor the word of a soothsayer﴾.

Which oath is greater? ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede (15), that run and hide (16), and by the night when it turns away (17), and by the morning when it breathes (18), that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (19), possessing power﴾, or: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger﴾ [al-Haqqah 38–40]. Which is greater?

The second is greater. Nothing is more general than it: ﴿what you see (38) and what you do not see﴾. All things either we see or we do not see. So Allah swore by everything. Here He swore by the heavenly signs, ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede (15) that run and hide﴾, and the night and the day, which are upper and horizontal signs. Look, glory be to Allah! It fits the messenger about whose word He swore, which is Jibril, because Jibril is with Allah.

If someone says: How does Allah describe the Qur'an as the word of a human messenger and of an angelic messenger? We say: Yes. The angelic messenger conveyed it to the human messenger, and the human messenger conveyed it to the nation. So it became the word of each by attribution: the word of Jibril by attribution, and the word of Muhammad by attribution. Who is the original first speaker? The first is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is Allah. So the Qur'an is truly the word of Allah, the word of Jibril in the sense that he conveyed it to Muhammad, and the word of Muhammad in the sense that he conveyed it to the nation. Is this clear, brothers?

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾ [at-Takwir 22]. Who is meant by "your companion"? Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Notice that He said ﴿your companion﴾ and did not say "Muhammad," as if to say: your companion whom you know, and whom you are always with, a companion who remained among them for forty years in Makkah before prophethood, whom they knew, and knew his truthfulness and trustworthiness, to the point that they called him "the Trustworthy."

﴿Your companion is not a madman﴾ means he is not mad. Rather, he is the most intelligent of the intelligent (peace be upon him), without doubt the most complete of people in intellect and the soundest in judgment.

﴿And your companion is not a madman. And he certainly saw him﴾ means he saw Jibril, ﴿on the clear horizon﴾, meaning the manifest, clear, and high horizon. The Messenger (peace be upon him) saw Jibril in the form in which he was created twice: once in the cave of Hira', and once in the seventh heaven when he was taken up (peace be upon him).

﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon﴾ [at-Takwir 23]. Which of these two sightings is this? ﴿He saw him on the clear horizon﴾: is it the sighting in the cave of Hira', or the sighting above the heavens? It is in the cave of Hira', because He says ﴿on the horizon﴾, so Muhammad was on earth.

﴿And he is not withholding of the unseen﴾ [at-Takwir 24], meaning Muhammad ﷺ is not, ﴿of the unseen﴾, meaning of the revelation that came to him from Allah, ﴿accused﴾, ﴿zanin﴾ with a ẓā' (ظنين) meaning accused, and there is a reading with ḍād (ضنين) meaning stingy.

He (peace be upon him) is neither accused regarding the revelation nor stingy with it. Rather, he is the most generous of people in conveying what was revealed to him. He teaches people on every occasion, and he is the furthest of people from accusation, because of the perfection of his truthfulness (peace be upon him).

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾ [at-Takwir 25], meaning it is not the word of any of the devils, who are the soothsayers to whom the devils reveal revelation, and they lie along with it and tell people, who then believe them to be truthful.

Then He said: ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 27].

We will leave the rest of the surah for another session.

* * *

Just as we have followed this method before, we will continue to follow it now and consistently, God willing, as long as no other method more complete than it is found, for a person seeks perfection to the extent he is able.

Last week we spoke about Surah at-Takwir, ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, until we reached the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And he is not withholding of the unseen (24). And it is not the word of an accursed devil (25). So where are you going?﴾ [at-Takwir 24–26].

(...) We continue here what we discussed earlier from Surah at-Takwir, where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede, (15) that run and hide,﴾ [at-Takwir 15–16]. Allah's words ﴿So I swear﴾ may lead some people to think that "la" is a negation, but it is not. Rather, it is an affirmation of the oath, and it is used in this structure for emphasis.

So the meaning is: ﴿I swear by the stars that recede﴾. Al-Khunnas (the stars that recede) is the plural of khanisah, which refers to stars that recede, meaning they return. You see them high on the horizon, and then they are suddenly moving back toward the other horizon. This is, and Allah knows best, because of their height and distance, so the stars beneath them appear, to the eye, to move faster than them.

As for His words ﴿al-jawari﴾, the original form is (al-jawari) with a yā', but the yā' was dropped for lightness. Al-Kunnas are those that hide (yakunisu), that is, they enter into their setting. Allah swore by these stars, then He swore by the night and the day, saying: ﴿And by the night when it turns away, (17) and by the morning when it breathes,﴾ [at-Takwir 17–18].

As for the meaning of ﴿'as'asa﴾: it means it approached (aqbala). It was also said that it means it withdrew (adbara). The word ʿasʿasa in the Arabic language is suitable for both, but what appears to be its meaning is "it approached," to match and agree with what follows it of the oath, which is His words ﴿and by the morning when it breathes﴾.

So Allah swore by the night as it approaches, and by the day as it approaches. Allah the Exalted swore by these creations because of their greatness and because they are among His great signs. Who can bring the day when it is night, and who can bring the night when it is day?

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If Allah were to make the night continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen? (71) Say: Have you considered? If Allah were to make the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see? (72) And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas 71–73].

These great creations are the things Allah swears by, because of the greatness of what is sworn to, which is His words: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [at-Takwir 19]. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿The word of a noble messenger﴾ is Jibril (peace be upon him), for he is the messenger of Allah to the messengers, with the revelation that he sends down to them. Allah described him as noble because of his good appearance, as He said in another verse: ﴿Possessor of strength; so he stood firm﴾ [an-Najm 6]. ﴿Possessor of strength (dhu mirrah)﴾: the scholars said that mirrah means good character and beautiful form. So Jibril (peace be upon him) was described with this description, ﴿noble﴾.

﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne﴾ [at-Takwir 20]. ﴿Possessing power﴾: Allah described him with great strength. The Messenger ﷺ saw him in his true form, in which Allah created him, having six hundred wings, which filled the whole horizon because of his greatness (peace be upon him).

His words ﴿near the Lord of the Throne﴾ mean near the Owner of the Throne, who is Allah, glorified and exalted. The Throne is above everything, and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Raised in degrees, Owner of the Throne; He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 15]. So the Owner of the Throne is Allah.

His words ﴿makin﴾ mean possessing standing, meaning that Jibril is, with Allah, of standing and honor. For this reason Allah singled him out with the greatest of the blessings that Allah sent down to His servants, which is revelation. My brothers, if we look at blessings, we will find that they are of two kinds: blessings in which animals and humans are equal, which are the enjoyment of the body: eating, drinking, marriage, and shelter. Humans are equal to animals in these blessings. Is that not so? Humans enjoy what they eat, what they drink, what they marry, and where they live, and animals are likewise.

The other blessings, which are specific to humans, are the laws (sharai'), the laws that Allah sent down through the messengers so that the lives of creation may be upright, because the lives of creation cannot be upright or good except through the laws: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97].

The believer who does righteous deeds is the one who has a good life in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter. By Allah, if you searched through kings and the sons of kings, ministers and the sons of ministers, rulers and the sons of rulers, the wealthy and the sons of the wealthy, and if you searched them and searched those who believed and did righteous deeds, you would find the second to have the better life, the more content heart, and the more open chest. This is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, has guaranteed it. He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

You find the believer who does righteous deeds joyful of heart, open of chest, content with Allah's decree and destiny. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke the truth.

So the greatest blessing Allah sent down to creation is the blessing of the religion, by which the life of a person is sustained in this world and the Hereafter. Now I ask you: What is life? Is it the life of this world or the life of the Hereafter? It is the life of the Hereafter. The evidence is His words in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life"﴾... Complete the verse: ﴿[Fajr 24]﴾, ["I wish I had sent forth (good) for my life"] [al-Fajr 24].

So this world is nothing; true life is the life of the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter will live a good life in this world, as I recited the verse to you. Thus the believer who does righteous deeds is the one who gains both lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is the one who loses both this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne. Jibril is the one who is obeyed, so who obeys him?

The scholars said: The angels obey him, because he descends with the command from Allah and then commands the angels, and they obey. So he has authority and obedience over the angels. Then the messengers (peace be upon them), to whom Jibril descends with revelation, have authority and obedience over the mukallafun (those obligated by the law). ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. The first is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is Allah. Is this clear, brothers?

﴿Your companion is not a madman﴾ means he is not mad. Rather, he is the most intelligent of the intelligent (peace be upon him), without doubt the most complete of people in intellect and the soundest in judgment.

He teaches people on every occasion, and he is the furthest of people from accusation, because of the perfection of his truthfulness (peace be upon him).

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾ [at-Takwir 25], meaning it is not the word of any of the devils, who are the soothsayers to whom the devils reveal revelation, and they lie along with it and tell people, who then believe them to be truthful.

Then He said: ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 27].

If Allah were to make the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see? (72) And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas 71–73].

These great creations are the things Allah swears by, because of the greatness of what is sworn to, which is His words: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [at-Takwir 19]. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿The word of a noble messenger﴾ is Jibril (peace be upon him), for he is the messenger of Allah to the messengers, with the revelation that he sends down to them. Allah described him as noble because of his good appearance, as He said in another verse: ﴿Possessor of strength; so he stood firm﴾ [an-Najm 6]. ﴿Possessor of strength (dhu mirrah)﴾: the scholars said that mirrah means good character and beautiful form. So Jibril (peace be upon him) was described with this description, ﴿noble﴾.

﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne﴾ [at-Takwir 20]. ﴿Possessing power﴾: Allah described him with great strength. The Messenger ﷺ saw him in his true form, in which Allah created him, having six hundred wings, which filled the whole horizon because of his greatness (peace be upon him).

His words ﴿near the Lord of the Throne﴾ mean near the Owner of the Throne, who is Allah, glorified and exalted. The Throne is above everything, and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Raised in degrees, Owner of the Throne; He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 15]. So the Owner of the Throne is Allah.

His words ﴿makin﴾ mean possessing standing, meaning that Jibril is, with Allah, of standing and honor. For this reason Allah singled him out with the greatest of the blessings that Allah sent down to His servants, which is revelation. My brothers, if we look at blessings, we will find that they are of two kinds: blessings in which animals and humans are equal, which are the enjoyment of the body: eating, drinking, marriage, and shelter. Humans are equal to animals in these blessings. Is that not so? Humans enjoy what they eat, what they drink, what they marry, and where they live, and animals are likewise.

The other blessings, which are specific to humans, are the laws (sharai'), the laws that Allah sent down through the messengers so that the lives of creation may be upright, because the lives of creation cannot be upright or good except through the laws: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97].

The believer who does righteous deeds is the one who has a good life in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter. By Allah, if you searched through kings and the sons of kings, ministers and the sons of ministers, rulers and the sons of rulers, the wealthy and the sons of the wealthy, and if you searched them and searched those who believed and did righteous deeds, you would find the second to have the better life, the more content heart, and the more open chest. This is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, has guaranteed it. He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

You find the believer who does righteous deeds joyful of heart, open of chest, content with Allah's decree and destiny. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke the truth.

So the greatest blessing Allah sent down to creation is the blessing of the religion, by which the life of a person is sustained in this world and the Hereafter. Now I ask you: What is life? Is it the life of this world or the life of the Hereafter? It is the life of the Hereafter. The evidence is His words in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life"﴾... Complete the verse: ﴿[Fajr 24]﴾, ["I wish I had sent forth (good) for my life"] [al-Fajr 24].

So this world is nothing; true life is the life of the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter will live a good life in this world, as I recited the verse to you. Thus the believer who does righteous deeds is the one who gains both lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is the one who loses both this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

The scholars said: The angels obey him, because he descends with the command from Allah and then commands the angels, and they obey. So he has authority and obedience over the angels. Then the messengers (peace be upon them), to whom Jibril descends with revelation, have authority and obedience over the mukallafun (those obligated by the law). ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. Then He said: ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 27].

His words ﴿near the Lord of the Throne﴾ mean near the Owner of the Throne, who is Allah, glorified and exalted. The Throne is above everything, and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Raised in degrees, Owner of the Throne; He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 15]. So the Owner of the Throne is Allah.

His words ﴿makin﴾ mean possessing standing, meaning that Jibril is, with Allah, of standing and honor. My brothers, if we look at blessings, we will find that they are of two kinds: blessings in which animals and humans are equal, which are the enjoyment of the body: eating, drinking, marriage, and shelter. Humans are equal to animals in these blessings. Is that not so? Humans enjoy what they eat, what they drink, what they marry, and where they live, and animals are likewise.

The other blessings, which are specific to humans, are the laws (sharai'), the laws that Allah sent down through the messengers so that the lives of creation may be upright, because the lives of creation cannot be upright or good except through the laws: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97].

The believer who does righteous deeds is the one who has a good life in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter. By Allah, if you searched through kings and the sons of kings, ministers and the sons of ministers, rulers and the sons of rulers, the wealthy and the sons of the wealthy, and if you searched them and searched those who believed and did righteous deeds, you would find the second to have the better life, the more content heart, and the more open chest. This is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, has guaranteed it. He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

You find the believer who does righteous deeds joyful of heart, open of chest, content with Allah's decree and destiny. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. The other blessings, which are specific to humans, are the laws (sharai'), the laws that Allah sent down through the messengers so that the lives of creation may be upright, because the lives of creation cannot be upright or good except through the laws: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl 97].

The believer who does righteous deeds is the one who has a good life in this world and a great reward in the Hereafter. By Allah, if you searched through kings and the sons of kings, ministers and the sons of ministers, rulers and the sons of rulers, the wealthy and the sons of the wealthy, and if you searched them and searched those who believed and did righteous deeds, you would find the second to have the better life, the more content heart, and the more open chest. This is because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, has guaranteed it. He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

You find the believer who does righteous deeds joyful of heart, open of chest, content with Allah's decree and destiny. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke the truth.

So the greatest blessing Allah sent down to creation is the blessing of the religion, by which the life of a person is sustained in this world and the Hereafter. Now I ask you: What is life? Is it the life of this world or the life of the Hereafter? It is the life of the Hereafter. The evidence is His words in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life"﴾... Complete the verse: ﴿[Fajr 24]﴾, ["I wish I had sent forth (good) for my life"] [al-Fajr 24].

So this world is nothing; true life is the life of the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter will live a good life in this world, as I recited the verse to you. Thus the believer who does righteous deeds is the one who gains both lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is the one who loses both this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne. Jibril is the one who is obeyed, so who obeys him?

The scholars said: The angels obey him, because he descends with the command from Allah and then commands the angels, and they obey. So he has authority and obedience over the angels. If good befalls him, he thanks Allah for it, and if the opposite befalls him, he is patient with it, seeks forgiveness from Allah for what he has done, knows that it befell him because of his sins, and returns to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "How wonderful is the affair of the believer; all of his affairs are good, and this is not so for anyone except the believer. If hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him."[[Narrated by Muslim (2999/64) from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]] And the Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke the truth.

So the greatest blessing Allah sent down to creation is the blessing of the religion, by which the life of a person is sustained in this world and the Hereafter. Now I ask you: What is life? Is it the life of this world or the life of the Hereafter? It is the life of the Hereafter. The evidence is His words in Surah al-Fajr: ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life"﴾... Complete the verse: ﴿[Fajr 24]﴾, ["I wish I had sent forth (good) for my life"] [al-Fajr 24].

So this world is nothing; true life is the life of the Hereafter. Whoever works for the Hereafter will live a good life in this world, as I recited the verse to you. Thus the believer who does righteous deeds is the one who gains both lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter, while the disbeliever is the one who loses both this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss﴾ [az-Zumar 15].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne. (20) Obeyed there and trustworthy﴾ [at-Takwir 20–21]. ﴿Obeyed there﴾ means there (in the heavens), ﴿trustworthy﴾ in what he was entrusted with. Who obeys him? Jibril is the one who is obeyed, so who obeys him?

The scholars said: The angels obey him, because he descends with the command from Allah and then commands the angels, and they obey. So he has authority and obedience over the angels. Then the messengers (peace be upon them), to whom Jibril descends with revelation, have authority and obedience over the mukallafun (those obligated by the law). ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾ [al-Ma'idah 92].

﴿Obeyed there and trustworthy﴾. When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, swore that this Qur'an is the word of this noble messenger, the angelic one, in another verse Allah clarified and swore that this Qur'an is the word of a noble messenger, in His words: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (40) and it is not the word of a poet﴾ [al-Haqqah 38–41]. Is the messenger there the same as the messenger here?

The answer: No. The messenger here, in Surah at-Takwir, is an angelic messenger, meaning one of the angels, and he is Jibril. The messenger there is a human messenger, and he is Muhammad (peace be upon him).

The evidence for this is clear. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger (19), possessing power, with rank near the Lord of the Throne﴾. To whom does this description refer? There He said: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (40) and it is not the word of a poet﴾, in response to the saying of the disbelievers who said that Muhammad is a poet, ﴿nor the word of a soothsayer﴾.

Which oath is greater? ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede (15), that run and hide (16), and by the night when it turns away (17), and by the morning when it breathes (18), that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger (19), possessing power﴾, or: ﴿So I swear by what you see (38) and what you do not see (39) that it is indeed the word of a noble messenger﴾ [al-Haqqah 38–40]. Which is greater?

The second is greater. Nothing is more general than it: ﴿what you see (38) and what you do not see﴾. All things either we see or we do not see. So Allah swore by everything. Here He swore by the heavenly signs, ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede (15) that run and hide﴾, and the night and the day, which are upper and horizontal signs. Look, glory be to Allah! It fits the messenger about whose word He swore, which is Jibril, because Jibril is with Allah.

If someone says: How does Allah describe the Qur'an as the word of a human messenger and of an angelic messenger? We say: Yes. The angelic messenger conveyed it to the human messenger, and the human messenger conveyed it to the nation. So it became the word of each by attribution: the word of Jibril by attribution, and the word of Muhammad by attribution. Who is the original first speaker? The first is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is Allah. So the Qur'an is truly the word of Allah, the word of Jibril in the sense that he conveyed it to Muhammad, and the word of Muhammad in the sense that he conveyed it to the nation. Is this clear, brothers?

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾ [at-Takwir 22]. Who is meant by "your companion"? Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Notice that He said ﴿your companion﴾ and did not say "Muhammad," as if to say: your companion whom you know, and whom you are always with, a companion who remained among them for forty years in Makkah before prophethood, whom they knew, and knew his truthfulness and trustworthiness, to the point that they called him "the Trustworthy."

﴿Your companion is not a madman﴾ means he is not mad. Rather, he is the most intelligent of the intelligent (peace be upon him), without doubt the most complete of people in intellect and the soundest in judgment.

﴿And your companion is not a madman. And he certainly saw him﴾ means he saw Jibril, ﴿on the clear horizon﴾, meaning the manifest, clear, and high horizon. The Messenger (peace be upon him) saw Jibril in the form in which he was created twice: once in the cave of Hira', and once in the seventh heaven when he was taken up (peace be upon him).

﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon﴾ [at-Takwir 23]. Which of these two sightings is this? ﴿He saw him on the clear horizon﴾: is it the sighting in the cave of Hira', or the sighting above the heavens? It is in the cave of Hira', because He says ﴿on the horizon﴾, so Muhammad was on earth.

﴿And he is not withholding of the unseen﴾ [at-Takwir 24], meaning Muhammad ﷺ is not, ﴿of the unseen﴾, meaning of the revelation that came to him from Allah, ﴿accused﴾, ﴿zanin﴾ with a ẓā' (ظنين) meaning accused, and there is a reading with ḍād (ضنين) meaning stingy.

He (peace be upon him) is neither accused regarding the revelation nor stingy with it. Rather, he is the most generous of people in conveying what was revealed to him. He teaches people on every occasion, and he is the furthest of people from accusation, because of the perfection of his truthfulness (peace be upon him).

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil﴾ [at-Takwir 25], meaning it is not the word of any of the devils, who are the soothsayers to whom the devils reveal revelation, and they lie along with it and tell people, who then believe them to be truthful.

Then He said: ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 27].

This is, and Allah knows best, because of their height and distance, so the stars beneath them appear, to the eye, to move faster than them.

Just as we have followed this method before, we will continue to follow it now and consistently, God willing, as long as no other method more complete than it is found, for a person seeks perfection to the extent he is able.

Last week we spoke about Surah at-Takwir, ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, until we reached the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And he is not withholding of the unseen (24). And it is not the word of an accursed devil (25). So where are you going?﴾ [at-Takwir 24–26].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 81, verses 27–29:

So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ (inna) carries the meaning of ﴿ma﴾ (negation). This is a rule: when ﴿illa﴾ (except) comes after ﴿in﴾, it has the meaning of ﴿ma﴾, meaning that it is a negation, because ﴿in﴾ comes as a negation, comes as a conditional, and comes as a lightened form of the heavy (inna). What clarifies these meanings is the context. When ﴿in﴾ is followed by ﴿illa﴾, it is a negation, i.e.: it (the Qur'an which Muhammad ﷺ brought and which Jibril descended with upon his heart) is not ﴿except a reminder to the worlds﴾.

﴿Reminder﴾ (dhikr) includes both admonishing and being reminded. So it is a reminder to the worlds and a remembrance for them, meaning that they are reminded by it and admonished by it. The intended meaning of "the worlds" is those to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 107], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan 1].

So the intended meaning of "the worlds" here is those to whom Muhammad ﷺ was sent.

He said: ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾ [at-Takwir 28]. ﴿For whoever wills﴾ is a substitute (badal) for what precedes it, but with the governing particle repeated, which is ﴿illa﴾ (except). That is: it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, for whoever among you wills to be upright. As for one who does not will uprightness, he will not be reminded by this Qur'an nor benefit from it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is present﴾ [Qaf 37]. So a person who does not want uprightness cannot benefit from this Qur'an.

But if someone says: Is a person's will by his own choice? We say: Yes, a person's will is by his own choice. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given man choice and volition: if he wills, he does; and if he wills, he does not. For if this were not so, the proof would not be established against the creatures to whom the messengers were sent by the sending of messengers. Have you understood the matter?

Is what we do by our own choice and volition? The answer: Yes, it is by our choice and volition, and were it not so, the sending of messengers would not be a proof against us; for we could say: "We are not able to choose." Man, without doubt, acts by his choice.

Every person knows that if he wants to go to Makkah, it is by his choice; if he wants to go to Madinah, it is by his choice; if he wants to go to Bayt al-Maqdis, it is by his choice; if he wants to go to Riyadh, it is by his choice, or to whatever he wishes, it is by his choice. He does not see that anyone compelled him to it, and he does not feel that anyone forced him to that.

Likewise, whoever wants to perform obedience to Allah, it is by his choice; and whoever wants to disobey Allah, it is by his choice. The will belongs to the person; he is free in it. But we know with certainty that he does not will anything except that Allah had willed it beforehand. Hence He said: ﴿And you will not, except that Allah wills﴾ [at-Takwir 29].

We do not will anything except after Allah has willed it. So when we will a thing, we know that Allah has willed it, and were it not that Allah willed it, we would not have willed it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them; but they differed, so among them were those who believed and among them those who disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another﴾ [al-Baqarah 253]. So when we do a thing, we do it by our will and choice, but we know that this will and choice came after the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and if Allah had willed, we would not have done it.

If someone says: Then do we have a proof in disobedience, since we only willed it after Allah had willed it?

The answer: We have no proof, because we did not know that Allah had willed it except after we had done it, and our doing it was by our choice. Hence we cannot say that Allah willed such-and-such, or willed such-and-such, except after it occurs. And when it occurs, by what does it occur? It occurs by our will and volition. Therefore it is not valid that the disobedient person has a proof against Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Allah has nullified this argument in His saying: ﴿Those who associated will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise denied those before them until they tasted Our punishment﴾ [al-An'am 148]. Had there been no proof against them, Allah would not have made them taste His punishment; they tasted the punishment of Allah, but they had no proof, so they tasted the punishment of Allah.

We all know that if a person is told that there is a city secure and tranquil, whose provision comes to it abundantly from every place, with markets and livelihoods not found in other lands, and that another city is a fearful, unstable place, disturbed in its economy and disturbed in fear and security, to which of the two will he go? Certainly he will go to the first, without doubt, and he does not see that anyone compelled him to go to the first; he sees that he went to the first by his own free will.

Likewise now, the path of good and the path of evil: Allah has told us: this is the path of Hell and this is the path of Paradise, and He has explained to us what is in Paradise of bliss and what is in the Fire of punishment. So which of them do we take? By clear and evident analogy, we will take the path of what? The path of Paradise, without doubt, just as in the previous example we take the path of the secure city whose provision comes to it abundantly from every place.

If we were to take the path of the Fire, there would be blame, rebuke and reproach upon us, and we would be called foolish, just as if in the first example we took the path of the fearful, unstable city where there is no stability; everyone would blame and rebuke us.

Thus in His saying: ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾ there is an affirmation that man does a thing by what? By his will and choice. But after he does the thing and wills the thing, we know that Allah had willed it beforehand, and had Allah willed, he would not have done it.

Often a person resolves upon something, and after the resolution he finds himself turned away from it, or finds himself diverted from it, because Allah did not will it.
