Rather, by the pure will of Allah, the aspirations are turned: a person sets his mind upon a thing and turns entirely toward it, and then finds himself turned away from it, whether the turning away is a physical obstacle or merely a choice that the person made to turn away. All of this is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

So the conclusion is that Allah says: ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾. And what is the meaning of uprightness? Uprightness is moderation, and there is no justice more upright than the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His law. In the earlier laws, the laws suited the circumstances of the nations in time, place and condition.

After the mission of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, his law suited the nation to which the Prophet ﷺ was sent, from the beginning of his mission until the end of the world. Hence it is among the well-known expressions: the Islamic religion is suitable for every time, place and condition; if people adhered to it, Allah would set the creation right.

Consider, for example, the person who prays: first standing, then if he is unable, sitting, then if he is unable, on his side. So the law adapts according to the condition of the person, because the religion is suitable for every time and place. The one who has become impure must purify himself with water; if the use of water is impossible due to inability or absence, he turns to tayammum; if neither water nor earth is found, or he is unable to use earth, he prays without anything, neither purification by water nor purification by tayammum.

All of this is because the law of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is entirely built upon justice: there is no injustice in it, no oppression in it, no hardship in it, no difficulty in it. Hence He said: ﴿to be upright﴾. The opposite of uprightness is two deviations: a deviation toward excess and extremism, and a deviation toward laxity and negligence.

Hence people in the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are of three kinds: two extremes and a middle. One extreme is the zealous one who exaggerates, is over-strict, pedantic and rigid; the other extreme is the negligent one who is lax, careless and neglectful; and the third is the middle between excess and laxity, upright upon the religion of Allah. This is the one who is praised. As for the first and the second, the first being the zealot and the second the neglectful, both are destroyed, each according to the extremism or the negligence he has.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade extremism, excess, rigidity and pedantry, to the extent that he said: "The over-pedantic are destroyed, the over-pedantic are destroyed, the over-pedantic are destroyed" [Narrated by Muslim (2670/7) from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him]; for pedantry involves hardship upon the self and departure from the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Just as he censured the negligent and careless, and said in describing the hypocrites: ﴿And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily﴾ [an-Nisa' 142].

So the religion of Allah is moderate between its zealot and its neglecter. Hence He said here: ﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, who does not incline to the right or the left, whose course is a course of uprightness upon the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Uprightness, as it is in dealing with the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, which is worship, is also in dealing with the creation.

So be among people between two extremes: between the extremes of harshness, severity and frowning, and the extreme of laxity, negligence, giving up oneself and lowering one's rank. Be firm in one respect and gentle in another. Hence the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, said regarding the judge: he should be gentle without weakness, strong without harshness, so that his gentleness does not lead him to weakness and his strength does not lead him to harshness; he should be between these, gentle without weakness, strong without harshness, so that affairs may be set right.

Some people, for example, always deal with others with frowning and severity, giving themselves the impression that they are above people and that people are beneath them; this is an error. And some people demean themselves and are humble to the point of laxity and indifference, so that they remain among people without any respect; this too is an error.

What is obligatory is that a person be between these two, as is the guidance of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for he was firm where firmness was called for and gentle where gentleness was called for. Thus a person combines here resolve and determination with gentleness, tenderness and mercy.

﴿for whoever among you wills to be upright﴾, and ﴿And you will not, except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir 29]: meaning, you cannot will anything except that Allah had willed it beforehand. So my will now to speak and address you is my own will, but it was only after the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Had Allah willed, I would not have willed; and had Allah willed that a thing not be, it would not be, even if I willed it. Even if I will and Allah the Exalted does not will, it will not happen; rather Allah brings about causes that stand between me and it, so that it does not occur.

This is a matter that a person must be attentive to: that he knows his act is by his will, a complete will without compulsion, but this will is joined to what? To the will of Allah. He knows that he did not will a thing except after Allah had willed it, and that if Allah had willed that it not be, the person would not have willed it, or the person would have willed it but Allah would have stood between him and it through causes and obstacles.

﴿And you will not, except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds.﴾ Here He said: ﴿And you will not, except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ and did not say "your Lord," indicating the generality of Allah's lordship, and that the lordship of Allah the Exalted is general. But you must know that ﴿the worlds﴾ here is not like the worlds in His saying: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾. I said regarding the first "the worlds" that the intended meaning is what? Those to whom the Messenger was sent. But here, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾.

The intended meaning of ﴿the worlds﴾ here is everything other than Allah; everything other than Allah is a world, for there is nothing but a Lord and a thing that is lordled. So when it is said "Lord of the worlds," it is determined that the intended meaning of "the worlds" is everything other than Allah, as the Imam, the Shaykh of Islam Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Everything other than Allah is a world, and I am one of that world."

The conclusion is that this surah is a great surah, containing a reminder and an admonition which the believer should recite with reflection and deliberation, and be admonished by what is in it. Likewise, it is obligatory upon him, in all the surahs and verses of the Qur'an, to be so, until he becomes one of those who are admonished by the Book of Allah and benefit from it.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to admonish us and you by His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and His signs in the universe, for He is capable of all things. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, all of them.
